entities.summary: Grover Cleveland's second tenure as the president of the United States began on March 4, 1893, when he was inaugurated as the nation's 24th president, and ended on March 4, 1897. Cleveland, a Democrat from New York, who previously served as 22nd president from 1885 to 1889 and lost re-election to Benjamin Harrison, a Republican from Indiana, in the 1888 presidential election, took office following his victory over incumbent President Harrison in the 1892 presidential election. Cleveland was the first former U.S. president to return to office. He was succeeded by Republican William McKinley.
